experiment_cards.title: Example 12 / SEQ17: receptor cAMP potency under FBS/BSA conditions
experiment_cards.experiment_system: Functional cAMP response in HEK-293 clonal cell lines overexpressing human GcgR, GIPR or GLP-1R; separate receptor cell lines

sample_size.unit_definition: Biological versus technical repeats and independent days/preparations not specified on the reviewed pages

assay_conditions.medium: DMEM with 1X GlutaMAX, 250 uM IBMX and 20 mM HEPES
assay_conditions.quantification: cAMP standard curve followed by normalization to native ligand maximal response; relative EC50 from four-parameter logistic regression

experiment_cards.comparator: Native human glucagon, GIP(1-42)NH2 and GLP-1(7-36)NH2; summary control measurements are not a randomized clinical comparator
experiment_cards.endpoint: Relative functional cAMP EC50 in each separately overexpressed receptor cell line
experiment_cards.unit: nM for EC50 and SEM; n is reported assay repeats with independent unit unspecified

Human clinical endpoint and clinical effect estimate

source_discrepancies.action: Use original page value; archived OCR is retained unchanged

source_discrepancies.location: PDF29 native controls and PDF30 Table3 note
source_discrepancies.detail: Reported native-control EC50 values 0.0125/0.133/0.0591 nM are below the printed native range lower bound 448 pM (0.448 nM). Cause is unexplained; printed units are not repaired. Example12 values lie within its separately stated example range.

experiment_cards.interpretation_limit: Reported engineered-cell potency supports a mechanism hypothesis only. It does not establish clinical efficacy, patient exposure, safety, trial success probability or patent rights. Table4 casein-condition values, Table2 binding Ki and Example1 mouse values are excluded from this card.

Example 3 — Safety Evaluation of Antibody Drug Conjugates

[0418] The antibody-drug conjugates (1) and (2) produced according to Example 1 were separately
administered to a cross-reactive species, cynomolgus monkeys. More specifically, the antibody-
drug conjugate (1) was administered at intervals of once in every three weeks, three times in total;
whereas, the antibody-drug conjugate (2) was administered at intervals of once a week, twice in
total. In the case of the antibody-drug conjugate (1), observation was continued up to the following
day of the final administration. In the case of the antibody-drug conjugate (2), observation was
continued up to the following week of the final administration. As a result, the highest non-
severely toxic dose (HNSTD) of the antibody-drug conjugate (2) was less than 10 mg/kg; whereas,
the HNSTD of the antibody-drug conjugate (1) was 30 mg/kg. Thus, it was demonstrated that the
antibody-drug conjugate (1) has better safety than the antibody-drug conjugate (2).

Example 5 — Initial Phase 1 Clinical Study

[0421] Introduction

[0422] DS-1062a is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-targeting antibody-drug
conjugate with a novel topoisomerase I inhibitor (Exatecan derivative; DXd). DS-1062a binds to
TROP2 on the cell surface, internalizes and releases DXd into the cytoplasm after enzymatic

processing which inhibits topoisomerase I and leads to apoptosis of the target cells.

[0423] TROP2 is highly expressed in epithelial cancers, including lung cancer, and is associated
with poor survival. In preclinical studies, DS-1062a showed promising antitumor activity in

xenograft mouse models.
[0424] Purpose

[0425] The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and tolerability of DS-1062a and
determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and recommended dose for expansion (RDE) (see
clinicaltrials. gov identifier NCT03401385).

[0426] Study Design and Methods

[0427] The Phase 1 study was a multicenter, open-label, multiple-dose, first-in-human study of DS-

escalation arm and a dose expansion arm, as shown in Figure 5. The dose escalation arm included
a single intravenous infusion of DS-1062a and a 21-day dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) observation

Example 7 — Preliminary Efficacy of Antibody Drug Conjugate

[0455] As of 16 Nov 2019, 88 of the 95 subjects that had been treated with DS-1062a were

evaluable for response

[0456] The investigator-assessed overall response rate (ORR; unconfirmed) was 27.8% (95% CI:
9.7, 53.5) in the 6 mg/kg dose group (5/18 subjects with response, all with PR) and 38.2% (95% CI
22.2, 56.4) in the 8 mg/kg dose group (13/34, all with PR) (Table 2 and Figure 22). The disease
control rate (DCR=CR+PR+SD) was 72.2% in 6 mg/kg and 79.4% in 8 mg/kg.

[0457] At the data cut-off date, all 5 subjects with PR in the 6 mg/kg dose group were ongoing on

treatment without disease progression or death

[0458] In the 8 mg/kg dose group, 6 of 13 subjects with PR were ongoing on treatment without
disease progression or death; 2 had progressive disease; 1 died; and 4 discontinued the DS-1062a

due to reasons other than disease progression or death.
